subject: platform/llm
professional: a senior platform / ML infrastructure engineer who owns the LLM gateway for a company: they would first ask whether token accounting matches what each provider bills (because a spend cap is only as good as its usage numbers), whether any code path can reach a paid endpoint without an explicit key, and whether failures are surfaced rather than swallowed.

evidence.correctness: What it is: platform/llm/byok.mjs (281 lines), a zero-dependency multi-provider client (anthropic, openai, gemini, openai-compatible, ollama, lmstudio, llamacpp) with usage parsing, spend-guard hooks, detectLocal and withFallback. I drove it with an injected fetch (scratchpad p.mjs) and checked outputs against sources the author did not write. (1) Spend-guard charge: with prices in 5 and out 25 per million, 100 in and 400 out must cost 100*5/1e6 + 400*25/1e6 = 0.0105 USD by hand; the repo's guard test asserts spentUsd 0.0105 and it passed, and my own run showed the guard receiving usage {input:4,output:2} and max_tokens clamped from 2048 to 50. (2) Anthropic usage, against Anthropic's documented usage object: input_tokens 10 + cache_read 100 + cache_creation 50 returned input 160. That is a documented over-count when charged at the full input rate (cache reads bill at 0.1x, writes at 1.25x), so the cap errs safe but the cost is wrong. (3) Gemini, against Google's documented usageMetadata: candidatesTokenCount excludes thoughtsTokenCount, and thinking tokens are billed as output. With candidates 3 and thoughts 900 the client reported output 3, a 300x under-count for a thinking model, so the guard under-charges Gemini 2.5 style calls. (4) isLocal probe of 10 URLs: 172.15 false, 172.16 true, localhost.evil.com false, 10.0.0.1.evil.com false, 169.254.x false, fd00::1 false (conservative), foo.local true: correct on the cases that matter for the 'stays on your computer' claim. (5) configFromEnv({OLLAMA_HOST:'[::1]'}) returned http://[::1]/v1: the port 11434 is dropped because the 'has a port' regex matches inside the IPv6 literal, so the call goes to port 80 (real bug, reproduced). Recomputation here was by hand and by injected responses, not against live providers, and wire formats were compared with the providers' public docs from memory, not fetched.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked by running: seven providers with correct endpoint and auth header (anthropic x-api-key, gemini x-goog-api-key, bearer for the rest, tests 15 to 37 and 52 passed); default model only for anthropic (config test); key-optional local presets and ollama/lmstudio/llamacpp default ports (test 165); configFromEnv incl. OLLAMA_HOST and LLM_PROVIDER (ran it); listModels and detectLocal (tests plus scratch run); isLocal; withFallback returns source 'fallback' with no key and made 0 fetch calls in my run; spend guard before-send refusal, ceiling clamp, settle, cancel (ran against the real createGuard in ventures/llm-spend-guard). All claimed features work. Not claimed and absent: streaming, retries, tool use, images (README says images are deliberately not built). 17 copies of byok.mjs elsewhere in ventures/platform are byte-identical to the source (cmp: same=17 drift=0).
evidence.verification: Ran: node --test '*.test.mjs' in platform/llm, 22 pass 0 fail, 213 ms, no network. Seeded 4 mutations, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean afterwards). M1 drop cache_creation_input_tokens from the Anthropic usage sum: CAUGHT (1 fail). M4 change retryable 429 to 428: CAUGHT. M2 remove the guard.cancel(hold) in the network-throw path (fetch rejects): SURVIVED, 22 pass, so a hold leak on a network failure, which would permanently consume budget, is untested (the existing test covers only the HTTP-error cancel). M3 make the Gemini request ignore maxTokens (hard-code 2048, which also bypasses the guard's output ceiling for Gemini): SURVIVED, 22 pass, because the gemini test never asserts generationConfig.maxOutputTokens. Two of four seeded bugs, both on the cost-control path, went undetected. Tests also never feed a Gemini thinking response, a blocked or empty response, or an IPv6 OLLAMA_HOST.
evidence.craft: Read byok.mjs in full and byok.test.mjs headers. Good: single file, no dependencies, injected fetch for tests, ByokError with retryable and status, never echoes a response body, key in header not URL for Gemini, AbortSignal plumbing, detectLocal never rejects and clears timers, settle(hold,null) on a 200 with unparsable body (charges conservatively). Defects: empty text is returned as success for a Gemini promptFeedback block, a null OpenAI content or a finish_reason of length with no content, so withFallback reports source 'model' with an empty value instead of falling back (reproduced); maxTokens 0 is sent as is; a thrown network error message is passed through verbatim into ByokError (fetch errors rarely contain the key, but it is not scrubbed); configFromEnv throws instead of returning null when LLM_PROVIDER names a provider with a missing key or model, contradicting its own doc comment 'null when nothing is configured' (reproduced for OLLAMA_HOST with no model, and LLM_PROVIDER=openai with only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set).
evidence.claims: Each README claim checked: no dependencies and plain fetch (grep fetch, only globalThis.fetch, true); only Anthropic has a default model (true); errors never echo a provider body (true, ran a 4xx/5xx test); 'real usage is charged afterwards' (true for Anthropic and OpenAI shapes, not for Gemini thinking tokens, see correctness); 'A call that would cross a budget is refused before it is sent' (true, sent counter unchanged in the test and in my run); 'output cap is lowered to the policy ceiling' (true for OpenAI-shaped and Anthropic requests, false for Gemini because maxOutputTokens there is the caller value, though in the code it is passed through correctly from the clamped maxTokens, so the unaffected path is covered; only the untested mutation exposes the risk); isLocal 'private addresses' (true for RFC1918, localhost, .local; link-local and ULA return false, narrower than 'private' but safe). Default model id claude-opus-5-5 could not be verified here (no network lookup done). Test command in README works. The README says 'duncan-haywood.github.io' in an OLLAMA_ORIGINS example, whereas CLAUDE.md says the catalogue moved to marisstella.app (stale, low).
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a venture author wants BYOK with a free fallback and a spend cap. Ran configFromEnv({}) -> null; withFallback(null) and withFallback({provider:'openai'}) with no key -> deterministic value, source fallback, zero network calls; Anthropic key -> complete works with injected fetch and guard clamps. 17 callers already use the identical file (grep, cmp), so it is demonstrably useful. Gaps a gateway owner hits in the first hour: no retry or backoff despite returning a retryable flag, no streaming, no per-call timeout (caller must pass a signal), no distinction of an empty or blocked reply.
evidence.domain: Compared with provider API docs and with what a gateway such as LiteLLM or the Vercel AI SDK does: they normalise reasoning/thinking and cache tokens into billed units, surface finish_reason and safety blocks, and ship retry policy. This client normalises only input/output and merges cache tokens at full price, and drops Gemini thinking tokens, so the cost number a spend guard sees is not the billed number for two of three hosted providers. Credit: the browser-direct header opt-in for Anthropic is explicit, and the key switch is sound (see below). A practitioner would adopt it for simple prompt-in text-out calls but would not trust its usage figures for budget enforcement without the fixes.

defects.what: Gemini usage ignores usageMetadata.thoughtsTokenCount, which Google bills as output; reproduced output 3 reported for a call with 900 thinking tokens. The spend guard therefore under-charges Gemini thinking models and can let a budget be overrun.

Anthropic cache read and creation tokens are summed into input at the full input price (160 reported for 10+100+50), so cost is overstated (reads bill at 0.1x, writes 1.25x); safe direction but wrong, and no way to price them separately.
Seeded mutations survived: removing guard.cancel on the network-throw path, and making the Gemini request ignore maxTokens (bypassing the guard's output ceiling for Gemini). No test asserts either.

Empty or blocked replies (Gemini promptFeedback block, null OpenAI content, length stop with no content) resolve as success with text '', so withFallback labels source 'model' with an empty value and never falls back.
ollamaBase drops the default port for a bracketed IPv6 host: OLLAMA_HOST=[::1] gives http://[::1]/v1 (port 80), because the has-a-port regex matches the colons in the literal.

configFromEnv throws ByokError for a named provider with missing key/model although its doc says null when nothing is configured; callers using withFallback(configFromEnv(env)) crash instead of falling back.
README OLLAMA_ORIGINS example names the retired GitHub Pages origin; isLocal treats link-local and ULA IPv6 as non-local (conservative); no retry, streaming, or default timeout.

verdict: A small, clean, dependency-free client whose tests pass (22 of 22) and whose structure is right, with a key switch that holds: I verified no paid call can be made without an explicit key. normalise() throws for anthropic, openai and gemini when apiKey is absent (keyRequired true), withFallback checks isConfigured first and made zero fetch calls without a key, configFromEnv returns null with an empty env, the only default base URLs are the providers' own, and the key-optional paths are the three localhost presets and openai-compatible, which requires a caller-supplied baseUrl. It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 because two of four seeded bugs on the cost-control path (network-failure hold release, Gemini output cap) were not caught, and correctness is 2 because usage accounting, the number the spend guard depends on, misses Gemini thinking tokens (under-charge) and over-charges Anthropic cache tokens; those are the reproduced defects a gateway engineer would find first. Scores are before any fix.
